scenes.title: Asymmetric Power: Rights Without Obligations
scenes.purpose: Futures impose mutual symmetric obligations; options grant unilateral rights without obligation
takeaways: Futures impose mutual symmetric obligations; options grant unilateral rights without obligation
The option buyer pays an upfront premium to buy asymmetric upside with capped downside
Chapter 10 explores exchange contract specifications, splits, dividends, and margin plumbing

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Throughout our study of futures and forward contracts, we operated in a world of strictly symmetric obligations: both buyer and seller are legally bound to execute the transaction at maturity, regardless of how far the market moves against them. Options introduce an entirely revolutionary financial architecture: unlimited upside potential with strictly bounded downside risk.

hi.display: Ab tak humne Futures aur Forwards study kiye, jo symmetric commitments the: Maturity par dono parties ko trade execute karna mandatory tha, chahe market kitna bhi against kyun na chala jaye. Lekin finance mein ek aisa instrument invent hua jo buyer ko unlimited upside deta hai aur downside risk ko completely eliminate karta hai: The Option Contract.

beats.onScreenIntent: Asymmetric Power: Rights Without Obligations

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: An Option is a contract that grants the buyer the legal right—but never the obligation—to buy or sell a specified quantity of an underlying asset at a fixed strike price, on or before an agreed expiration date.

hi.display: Option ek aisi financial derivative security hai jo buyer ko right yaani adhikar deti hai—lekin koi obligation yaani majboori nahi deti—ki wo specified strike price par underlying asset ko buy ya sell kar sake.

beats.onScreenIntent: Asymmetric Power: Rights Without Obligations

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In Part One of Chapter Ten, we will master the foundational Call and Put building blocks, examine American versus European exercise conventions, formulate the moneyness taxonomy, decode standardized exchange expiration cycles, and derive the exact mathematical adjustments for stock splits and corporate actions.

hi.display: John C. Hull ke Chapter Ten Part One mein hum Call aur Put options ke fundamental mechanics, Moneyness taxonomy, standardized expiration cycles, aur stock splits ke mathematical adjustments ko master karenge.

scenes.title: The Four Foundational Option Positions
scenes.purpose: Long Call: right to buy (capped loss = premium, unlimited upside potential)
takeaways: Long Call: right to buy (capped loss = premium, unlimited upside potential)
Short Call: obligation to sell (capped gain = premium, unlimited downside liability)
Long Put: right to sell (downside hedge), Short Put: obligation to buy (downside exposure)

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The vast universe of options trading and quantitative strategies is built upon four foundational positions: Long Call, Short Call, Long Put, and Short Put.

hi.display: Options trading mein chaar foundational building blocks hote hain jo pure market architecture ko define karte hain: Long Call, Short Call, Long Put, aur Short Put.

beats.onScreenIntent: The Four Foundational Option Positions

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: A Call Option gives the holder the right to buy the underlying asset at strike price K. A Put Option gives the holder the right to sell the underlying asset at strike price K. To acquire this valuable asymmetric right without an offsetting obligation, the option buyer pays an upfront, non-refundable cash fee called the Option Premium.

hi.display: Call Option buyer ko asset buy karne ka right deta hai, jabki Put Option buyer ko asset sell karne ka right deta hai. Is asymmetric privilege ko khareedne ke liye buyer seller ko ek non-refundable upfront cash payment karta hai jise Option Premium kehte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: The Four Foundational Option Positions

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The Option Writer, or seller, collects this cash premium upfront, but assumes a legally binding obligation to fulfill the contract if the buyer chooses to exercise. For the buyer, maximum loss is strictly capped at the initial premium paid, while the writer faces potentially unlimited liability.

hi.display: Option Seller ya Writer premium collect karta hai lekin symmetric obligation assume karta hai: Agar buyer contract exercise karta hai, toh seller ko har haal mein delivery deni ya leni padegi. Buyer ka maximum loss strictly premium tak capped rehta hai.

scenes.title: Exercise Style: American vs. European Options
scenes.purpose: American options can be exercised on any trading day prior to and including expiration
takeaways: American options can be exercised on any trading day prior to and including expiration
European options can only be exercised on the final expiration date itself
Exchange-traded equity options in the US are American; broad-market index options are European

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Based on when the holder possesses the legal authority to exercise, options are divided into two primary legal classifications: American Style and European Style.

hi.display: Options market mein exercise timing ke basis par do distinct legal styles hote hain: American Style aur European Style.

beats.onScreenIntent: Exercise Style: American vs. European Options

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: An American Option can be exercised by the holder on any business day up to and including the expiration date. Virtually all exchange-traded options on individual US equities are American-style contracts, offering continuous early-exercise flexibility.

hi.display: American Option ko contract expiration date tak kisi bhi business day par exercise kiya ja sakta hai. Ye holder ko early exercise ki complete flexibility deta hai. US exchange-traded stock options primarily American style hote hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Exercise Style: American vs. European Options

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In contrast, a European Option can only be exercised on the final expiration date itself. Broad market index options—such as those on the S&P 500—are typically European-style and settle in cash, preventing the operational friction of delivering thousands of individual stock certificates.

hi.display: Iske opposite, European Option ko sirf aur sirf final expiration date par hi exercise kiya ja sakta hai; beech mein exercise legally allowed nahi hota. S&P five hundred jaise broad market indices European style hote hain aur inka settlement purely cash mein hota hai.

scenes.title: The Moneyness Spectrum: ITM, ATM, and OTM
scenes.purpose: Intrinsic value is the immediate exercise payoff: max(S - K, 0) for calls, max(K - S, 0) for puts
takeaways: Intrinsic value is the immediate exercise payoff: max(S - K, 0) for calls, max(K - S, 0) for puts
Option price equals Intrinsic Value plus Time Value
OTM options have zero intrinsic value and trade purely on the probability of reaching the strike

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: At any moment during its lifetime, an option's market price consists of two distinct components: Intrinsic Value and Time Value. The relationship between the underlying spot price S and the strike price K is known as Moneyness.

hi.display: Har option contract ki value do components se banti hai: Intrinsic Value aur Time Value. Inke relationship ko Moneyness kaha jata hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: The Moneyness Spectrum: ITM, ATM, and OTM

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: An option is In-the-Money if it possesses positive intrinsic value—meaning immediate exercise would generate a cash payoff. For a call, this occurs when spot price S exceeds strike K. For a put, it occurs when spot price S falls below strike K. An option is At-the-Money when the spot price exactly equals the strike price.

hi.display: In-the-Money ya ITM contract wo hota hai jisme immediate intrinsic value hoti hai: Call ke liye jab spot price strike se bada ho, aur Put ke liye jab spot price strike se chhota ho. At-the-Money ya ATM tab hota hai jab spot price strike price ke exactly barabar ho.

beats.onScreenIntent: The Moneyness Spectrum: ITM, ATM, and OTM

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: An option is Out-of-the-Money when immediate exercise would produce zero payoff. For an out-of-the-money option, intrinsic value is exactly zero. Its entire market price consists purely of Time Value, reflecting the statistical probability that the underlying price might cross the strike before expiration.

hi.display: Out-of-the-Money ya OTM contract mein intrinsic value zero hoti hai. Iski market price purely Time Value par depend karti hai yaani is probability par ki future mein market favorable direction mein move ho sakta hai.

scenes.purpose: Equity options cover 100 shares per contract and settle via physical share delivery
takeaways: Equity options cover 100 shares per contract and settle via physical share delivery
Index options (SPX, NDX) settle in cash based on index closing levels
Futures options give the right to enter a futures contract at strike K with immediate mark-to-market

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: On modern global derivatives exchanges, options contracts trade actively across four major asset classes, each governed by specific settlement and operational conventions.

hi.display: Modern derivatives exchanges par options multiple broad asset classes par trade hote hain, jinme se har ek ke apne specific settlement rules hote hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Underlying Asset Classes: Equities, Currencies, Indices & Futures

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: First: Individual Stock Options, where one contract standardly covers one hundred shares of equity, settled via physical share delivery. Second: Stock Index Options, which track broad market benchmarks like the S&P 500, settling purely in cash based on an index multiplier.

hi.display: Individual Equity Options ek hundred shares ke lot size par trade hote hain aur physical delivery lead karte hain. Stock Index Options broad portfolios jaise Nifty ya S&P 500 par trade hote hain aur strictly cash settlement execute karte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Underlying Asset Classes: Equities, Currencies, Indices & Futures

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Third: Currency Options, utilized by multinational corporations to hedge foreign exchange exposures. Fourth: Futures Options, where exercising the option delivers an active futures contract position rather than the underlying physical commodity.

hi.display: Foreign Currency Options cross-border foreign exchange risk ko hedge karte hain, jabki Futures Options exercise hone par underlying asset ke bajaye ek active futures contract deliver karte hain.

scenes.title: Exchange Specifications: Strike Intervals & Expiration Cycles
scenes.purpose: Strikes are spaced at standardized intervals ($0.50, $1.00, $2.50, $5.00) around current stock price
takeaways: Strikes are spaced at standardized intervals ($0.50, $1.00, $2.50, $5.00) around current stock price
Expiration cycles include near-term months plus rotating quarterly cycle months (Jan/Feb/Mar)
Standard monthly options expire on the third Friday of each calendar month

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Because exchange-traded options are standardized instruments rather than privately negotiated over-the-counter contracts, options exchanges enforce strict rules governing strike price intervals and expiration dates.

hi.display: Exchange-traded options private contracts nahi hote; inki liquidity preserve karne ke liye exchanges strict Standardization Rules enforce karti hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Exchange Specifications: Strike Intervals & Expiration Cycles

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Strike prices are spaced at standardized increments—such as two dollars and fifty cents, or five dollars—bracketed around the current stock price. Expiration dates follow a rotating three-cycle schedule: the January Cycle, February Cycle, or March Cycle.

hi.display: Strikes predetermined intervals par set hote hain: jaise two point five dollars ya five dollar multiples. Expiration dates monthly cycles mein rotate hoti hain: Cycle One January, Cycle Two February, aur Cycle Three March.

beats.onScreenIntent: Exchange Specifications: Strike Intervals & Expiration Cycles

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Standard monthly equity options expire on the third Friday of the expiration month. Under exchange rules, four expiration months trade simultaneously: the current calendar month, the subsequent calendar month, and the next two cycle months, ensuring continuous short-term liquidity alongside intermediate hedging horizons.

hi.display: Har equity option contract standardly expiration month ke Third Friday ko expire hota hai. Kisi bhi time par current month, next month aur predetermined cycle months ke contracts parallelly screen par trade hote hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Exchange Specifications: Strike Intervals & Expiration Cycles

scenes.title: Corporate Actions: Mathematical Adjustment for Stock Splits
scenes.purpose: For an N-for-M stock split, post-split strike K' = K * (M / N)
takeaways: For an N-for-M stock split, post-split strike K' = K * (M / N)
The number of shares covered by the option increases to 100 * (N / M)
The total economic commitment (Strike * Shares) remains completely unchanged

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: When a publicly traded company executes a stock split or stock dividend, its share price drops mechanically overnight. To protect option holders from arbitrary value destruction, the Options Clearing Corporation implements exact mathematical adjustments.

hi.display: Jab ek company stock split announce karti hai, toh stock price drop ho jata hai. Option holder ko unfair loss se protect karne ke liye Options Clearing Corporation contract terms ko mathematically adjust karti hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Corporate Actions: Mathematical Adjustment for Stock Splits

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: For an N-for-M stock split, the new adjusted strike price K-star equals the old strike price multiplied by M divided by N. Simultaneously, the number of shares covered by the contract expands from one hundred to one hundred multiplied by N divided by M.

hi.display: N-for-M stock split ke liye rule dekhiye: Naya strike price purane strike price ko M divided by N se multiply karke divide kiya jata hai, aur contract shares ko N divided by M se multiply kiya jata hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Corporate Actions: Mathematical Adjustment for Stock Splits

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: For example, suppose an investor holds an eighty-dollar strike call covering one hundred shares. If the company declares a two-for-one stock split, the strike price is halved to forty dollars, while the contract now covers two hundred shares. Total cash commitment upon exercise remains exactly eight thousand dollars, preserving perfect economic neutrality.

hi.display: Maan lijiye ek investor ke paas eighty dollar strike ka ek call contract hai jo one hundred shares cover karta hai. Company two-for-one split karti hai. Naya strike price forty dollars ban jayega aur contract two hundred shares cover karega. Dollar commitment exactly eight thousand dollars neutral rehta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Corporate Actions: Mathematical Adjustment for Stock Splits

scenes.title: The Cash Dividend Dilemma: Why Regular Dividends are Unprotected
scenes.purpose: Exchange options are not adjusted for ordinary cash dividends
takeaways: Exchange options are not adjusted for ordinary cash dividends
On the ex-dividend date, the stock drops by the dividend amount
This ex-dividend drop decreases call values and increases put values, pricing into market premiums

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In contrast to stock splits, options exchanges enforce a critical, non-negotiable rule: Exchange-traded options are NOT adjusted for ordinary, regular cash dividends.

hi.display: Stock splits ke opposite, regular quarterly cash dividends ke liye exchange options contracts ko bilkul adjust nahi karti. Ye options finance ka ek critical rule hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: The Cash Dividend Dilemma: Why Regular Dividends are Unprotected

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: On the ex-dividend date, the stock price drops by approximately the cash dividend amount as cash leaves the firm's balance sheet. Because the strike price remains unchanged, call option holders suffer an uncompensated value loss, while put option holders receive a windfall gain.

hi.display: Jab ek stock Ex-Dividend date par open hota hai, toh stock price dividend amount ke barabar drop ho jata hai. Is drop ki wajah se call option holders ko direct loss hota hai aur put option holders ko unexpected benefit milta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: The Cash Dividend Dilemma: Why Regular Dividends are Unprotected

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Because options markets are forward-looking, option pricing models discount expected future dividends in advance: stocks paying high dividend yields systematically feature cheaper call premiums and more expensive put premiums.

hi.display: Market pricing is dividend impact ko advance mein factor karti hai: High dividend yield stocks par call option premiums cheaper quote hote hain aur put option premiums relatively expensive quote hote hain.

scenes.title: Case Study: The Gucci Extraordinary Dividend Exception
scenes.purpose: When cash dividends exceed a major threshold (e.g. 10% of stock price), they qualify as extraordinary
takeaways: When cash dividends exceed a major threshold (e.g. 10% of stock price), they qualify as extraordinary
In 2004, Gucci paid a huge 13.50 EUR extraordinary cash dividend
The exchange adjusted option strikes downwards by the extraordinary cash dividend amount to prevent unfair loss

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In Business Snapshot 10.1, John Hull highlights the most famous historical exception to the cash dividend rule: The Gucci Group extraordinary dividend of 1999.

hi.display: John C. Hull Business Snapshot ten point one mein standard dividend rule ka ek famous historical exception present karte hain: The Gucci Group Event.

beats.onScreenIntent: Case Study: The Gucci Extraordinary Dividend Exception

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: As part of a strategic corporate defense battle between LVMH and Pinault-Printemps-Redoute, Gucci declared a massive special cash dividend of two dollars and eighty-eight cents per share, representing over thirty percent of the company's entire market value.

hi.display: Nineteen-ninety-nine mein luxury brand Gucci ne ek massive extraordinary cash dividend announce kiya: two point eight eight dollars per share, jo stock price ka thirty percent se zyada tha!

beats.onScreenIntent: Case Study: The Gucci Extraordinary Dividend Exception

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Because a thirty percent unadjusted stock drop would have completely wiped out call option holders while delivering an unfair windfall to put writers, the OCC Securities Committee intervened, ruling that this was an extraordinary corporate restructuring dividend and reducing all option strike prices by exactly two dollars and eighty-eight cents.

hi.display: Kyunki yeh regular dividend nahi tha balki corporate restructuring payout tha, Options Clearing Corporation ne emergency exception banakar Gucci ke saare options contracts ke strike prices ko two point eight eight dollars se permanently reduce kar diya taaki call option buyers overnight wipe out na ho jayein.

scenes.title: Active Recall Scenario: Calculating Post-Split Option Adjustments
scenes.purpose: A 3-for-1 split reduces a $150 strike option to $50
takeaways: A 3-for-1 split reduces a $150 strike option to $50
The number of shares covered triples from 100 to 300 shares
Total exercise commitment remains exactly $50 * 300 = $15,000

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let us now apply our understanding of corporate action mechanics to solve a practical stock split adjustment problem. Carefully review the terms on screen.

hi.display: Chaliye ab ek practical stock split adjustment scenario solve karte hain. Screen par diye gaye parameters ko evaluate kijiye.

beats.onScreenIntent: Active Recall Scenario: Calculating Post-Split Option Adjustments

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: An investor holds a call option with a strike price of sixty dollars covering one hundred shares. The underlying company executes a three-for-one stock split. What are the adjusted strike price and the number of shares covered by the adjusted contract? Pause and consider.

hi.display: Ek investor sixty dollar strike price ka one call option contract hold karta hai jo one hundred shares cover karta hai. Company three-for-one stock split execute karti hai. Split ke immediately baad naya strike price aur contract shares kitne honge? Pause and consider.

beats.onScreenIntent: Active Recall Scenario: Calculating Post-Split Option Adjustments

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The correct answer is Option A: The adjusted strike price is twenty dollars, covering three hundred shares. Applying the formula: the new strike equals sixty dollars multiplied by one-third, which equals twenty dollars. The number of shares covered equals one hundred multiplied by three, which equals three hundred shares. The total exercise cost remains sixty dollars times one hundred, or six thousand dollars, maintaining exact dollar neutrality.

hi.display: Correct answer hai Option A: Strike price twenty dollars ho jayega aur contract three hundred shares cover karega. Calculation dekhiye: Naya strike barabar sixty guna one divided by three equals twenty dollars. Naye shares barabar one hundred guna three divided by one equals three hundred shares. Total exercise commitment neutral twenty times three hundred equals $6,000 rehta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Active Recall Scenario: Calculating Post-Split Option Adjustments

data.question: An investor holds a call option contract covering 100 shares of stock with a strike price of $150. The company executes a 3-for-1 stock split. What are the adjusted strike price and number of shares covered?
options: The equilibrium condition holds via continuous risk-neutral replication.
Expected asset drift determines contingent claim value directly.
Arbitrage bounds can be systematically violated in liquid markets.
Discrete binomial tree steps eliminate all underlying price variance.
data.explanation: In a 3-for-1 split: K' = $150 * (1/3) = $50. Deliverable shares Q' = 100 * (3/1) = 300 shares. Total value = $50 * 300 = $15,000, identical to pre-split $150 * 100.

en.display: On professional trading terminals, options contracts are identified through standardized Option Symbology Initiative, or OSI, identifiers.

hi.display: Trading terminals par options contracts standardized OSI symbols se represent hote hain jinhein read karna har professional trader ko aana chahiye.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: An OSI identifier combines the underlying root symbol, the expiration date in year-month-day format, a single letter denoting a Call or Put, and an eight-digit number specifying the exact dollar strike price.

hi.display: Option symbol mein underlying stock ticker, expiration year, month aur day, Call ya Put identifier, aur eight-digit format mein exact strike price embedded hoti hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Option Symbols & Quote Reading: Navigating Option Chains

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Trading desks monitor option chains displaying bids, asks, trading volume, and Open Interest. Open Interest represents the total number of outstanding contracts that have not yet been settled by closing transactions or physical delivery, serving as the definitive measure of institutional market liquidity.

hi.display: Option Chain screen par bids, offers, volume aur Open Interest display karti hai. Open Interest wo total number of outstanding contracts hote hain jo abhi tak close ya exercise nahi huye hain.

scenes.purpose: Options give unilateral rights to buyers while writers carry legal fulfillment obligations
takeaways: Options give unilateral rights to buyers while writers carry legal fulfillment obligations
Stock splits scale strikes down and shares up to maintain total dollar invariance
Ordinary cash dividends are unprotected, creating powerful early-exercise incentives on calls

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let us consolidate our mastery of Chapter Ten Part One through the four structural pillars of options market mechanics.

hi.display: Aaiye Chapter Ten Part One ke chaar foundational option principles ko consolidate karte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Summary Thread: Four Pillars of Option Contract Specifications

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Pillar One: Asymmetric Rights Architecture. The option buyer pays a non-refundable cash premium to acquire rights without obligations, while the writer assumes binding contractual duties.

hi.display: Pillar One: Asymmetric Rights. Buyer premium pay karke right acquire karta hai jabki writer premium collect karke absolute obligation assume karta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Summary Thread: Four Pillars of Option Contract Specifications

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Pillar Two: Moneyness and Value Decomposition. Market prices comprise intrinsic value and time value; out-of-the-money options consist purely of statistical time value.

hi.display: Pillar Two: Moneyness Taxonomy. Options ITM, ATM ya OTM hote hain; OTM contracts ki value purely time value par depend karti hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Summary Thread: Four Pillars of Option Contract Specifications

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Pillar Three: Corporate Action Neutrality. Stock splits adjust strike prices and share deliverables proportionally to ensure zero economic wealth transfer.

hi.display: Pillar Three: Corporate Action Neutrality. Stock splits par strike price aur shares proportionally adjust hote hain taaki dollar neutrality maintain rahe.

beats.onScreenIntent: Summary Thread: Four Pillars of Option Contract Specifications

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Pillar Four: Cash Dividend Friction. Exchange options do not adjust for regular quarterly dividends, systematically depressing call values and elevating put values.

hi.display: Pillar Four: Unprotected Dividend Reality. Regular cash dividends strike adjust nahi karte; ex-dividend price drops call values ko compress karti hain.
